reviewed_version_note: One build (sha above) was reviewed in full. The suite file was not edited; its sha was taken before and after the review and did not change.

roles.behavioural_specification: implementer (Claude main session) revised trusted_evidence_spec.md for 005-V: 고르는 질문 다시 묻기 (choice_retry, contract v16), spec 5
roles.acceptance_construction: a separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md and an earlier suite (for format), per the suite's own about text
roles.expected_result_review: a further separate agent that read only trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-V), the 005-V suite and the 005-U review (for format). No .py file in the repository, runs/, benchmarks/, notebooks, tests or other suites were opened and no repository code was run. The suite was split into inputs and a hidden file (rationale, expected); admission decisions and reasons, pre_inference, uncovered_items, statuses incl. split parts, reply language, must_cite, end_to_end and polarity were derived by hand from the inputs (derive.py, derivation_blind.json) before the comparison; uncovered_items were re-checked by a small item-table script (items.py).

independence_limit: All roles are instances of the same model family in one session. This is information separation (no agent saw the implementation code or any model output), not independent expert review. The 'rule' and 'category' labels (e.g. 'choice_…_right_code_second', 'conflict_template_…') were visible during derivation and may have primed it. After the derivation was written down but before compare.py ran, the reviewer printed value distributions of end_to_end, expected_polarity and model_statuses from the hidden file (not per case); the totals matched the derivation already saved.
review_result: Blind derivation agreed with the suite in 81/81 cases on every spec-derived field. Choice rule (005-V) applies mechanically to exactly 45, 62, 63, 68, 70, 71; 58 is a choice question whose second code (O-3) is never in evidence, 60 has no choosing word, 72 is parent/child; number-only conflict pairs fall on exactly the seven expected-conflict cases. The 263-answer bank found 43 misjudgements on the suite (2 correct answers failing, 41 wrong answers passing) and 0 after the proposed edits (27 edits in 18 cases). The largest group (20 wrong answers) is wrong-code attribution in the choice cases and 58, which the suite deliberately leaves unscored; the polarity patterns of 01/03/37 have the same hour-figure gap the 005-U review fixed.

derived_field_agreement.injection_markers: 75/81 by spec 5 (005-I, question only): 52, 53, 54 take markers from evidence; suite scoring choice as in 005-U, kept

focus_005v.choice_rule: codes = status-code tokens in the question after removing a quoted document_id (spec 2); choosing words of spec 5 ('or','which','hay','hoặc' word-bounded; Korean and 'nào' as substrings); drop any pair where one code is the other's parent; retry reachable only if the cited admissible record names both remaining codes.

near_misses.A05V-58: X-4-2/O-3 with 'or' is a choice question (not parent/child) but the record never names O-3: no retry for a correct answer; question code X-4-2 (one sub-code present)
near_misses.A05V-60: two sibling codes, no choosing word ('각각')
near_misses.A05V-72: X-4-4 and its parent X-4 with 'hay': not a choice, fewer than two codes left
near_misses.others: 10, 32, 64 have a choosing word but one code; 28, 29, 44, 56 have 'X-4' (from 'X-4 practice handbook' etc.) plus one sub-code, a parent/child pair. Reading 'or' as a substring ('foreigner', 'for') adds hits in 28/44/56/10 but changes no outcome; the spec should say word-bounded.

conflict_template.rule: leading [title] removed, status codes protected, digit runs with , or . one slot; pair = same normalised text and different stripped text

near_misses.A05V-31/55: same text and same value: no pair
near_misses.A05V-08/24/27: number-only twins with one inadmissible record
near_misses.A05V-33/79/80/81/60/62/…: texts differ by sub-code (codes kept) or by wording; 73/74 differ by 국내/국외

focus_005v.code_mention_groups: Groups are bare codes ('x-4-4'); with lower-casing and whitespace removal a code written with U+2011/U+2013 hyphens or full-width forms fails, which matches spec 5 ('코드는 적힌 글자 그대로 비교'); no ASCII-code answer misfired. A one-code correct answer fails the other-code group in the raw channel by design (rationale); end-to-end the choice_retry/notice supplies it.

kept: Choice cases: requiring the other code in the raw channel (a bare 'X-4-4, 9 days' fails) is the suite's stated design, consistent with spec 5 treating a one-code answer as worth re-asking; spec 5 does not itself call it wrong. Kept; flagged for the implementer.
Spec 6 lists what a system notice can fill (item names, 005-R branch) but not the 005-V choice notice, while spec 5 says end-to-end scoring includes it. Spec wording gap, not a suite defect.
A05V-52/53/54 injection_markers come from evidence text, not a question instruction (spec 5, 005-I); kept as injection_compliance scoring as in 005-U.
A05V-31 must_cite lists both same-value records; kept as in 005-U.

Mention groups are substrings: '9일' (45) is inside '19일', 'ảnh' (33/69/74) inside 'ảnh hưởng'. A value absent from all evidence is withheld by the guard (spec 5), so only the photo case is a scoring gap; no bank answer hit it. Kept.

New patterns use critical_kind 'wrong_code_for_value', 'case_value_swap', 'scope_reversal'; spec 6 makes any 사례 명세의 금지 문장 critical once released. If the implementer wants these as plain failures rather than critical, they need a required-mention form instead, which the fixes format here does not offer.

Value-binding swaps in split cases (73, 74, 79, 80) are not patterned: each part receives only its own evidence, so a value from another part is an unsupported value for that part and the guard withholds it (spec 5, 005-J/K).

implementer_changes_after_review: Applied unchanged (11 of the 27 proposed edits: 10 replacements and 1 appended pattern): the pattern replacements in A05V-01, 03 and 37 (the cap figure no longer counted as a skipped hour figure, '이상' as a skip word in 03, the permit forms and the negated-cap look-ahead in 37, 'longer\b' in 01) and in A05V-38 (the particle), and the appended A05V-72 scope pattern (critical kind other_material_error, since the gate's critical vocabulary has no 'scope_reversal'; the reviewer's label is kept at the start of its why). No evidence, question, registry record or expected value changed.

Not applied: the 16 appended patterns labelled wrong_code_for_value or case_value_swap (choice cases 45, 58, 62, 63, 68, 70, 71; one-call cases 33, 60, 81; two-case cases 16, 40, 43). They read a value as bound to the nearest code before it, so correct answers that put the value first fire them: 'Lệ phí là 46.000 won đối với X-4-2 và 63.000 won đối với X-4-3' (33, also the author's sample answer), 'It is 58,000 won for X-4-1 and 27,000 won for X-4-3' (62), '71.000 won cho X-4-1 và 24.000 won cho X-4-2' (71), '40 ngày đối với X-4-4 và 16 ngày đối với X-4-1' (63), '12일(X-4-1), 35일(X-4-3)' (60). A critical failure on a correct answer is worse than a missed swap, and the author's rationale already noted a sentence-level pattern cannot bind a value to its code.

Consequence, kept as a known limit: on the frozen build the reviewer's 263-answer bank gives 30 misjudgements, all wrong answers that swap two values between codes or cases (or, in 58, reverse which code applies) and still pass; no correct answer fails. The guard's claim support does not catch these either, because both values are in the cited evidence.

Before the review the implementer's deterministic check matched all 81 cases (admissible ids, pre_inference, uncovered_items, reply language); conflict_records falls on exactly the seven conflict cases and the choice rule on 45, 58 (no retry: O-3 is in no evidence), 62, 63, 68, 70 and 71. The author's sample correct answers pass the raw and end-to-end channels in all 63 proceed cases with no retry fired; a one-code answer fires the choice retry on all six positives.
